method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Fundal massage directly addresses atony, but feeding history, walking during haemorrhage and pressure on a pad are implausible competing interventions.
issues: Fundal massage directly addresses atony, but feeding history, walking during haemorrhage and pressure on a pad are implausible competing interventions.
proposedChanges: Compare fundal massage with bladder assessment, quantifying blood loss, and checking for genital trauma; preserve the narrow action-directed-at-boggy-uterus question.

items.assessment: Persistent bleeding despite a firm midline uterus appropriately broadens assessment beyond atony; tone-only reassurance and repeated massage are recognizable anchoring errors.
The seizure protection steps are correct but are direct first-aid recall despite the obstetric setting.
issues: The seizure protection steps are correct but are direct first-aid recall despite the obstetric setting.
proposedChanges: Classify foundation, and consider replacing the restraint-to-limit-oxygen rationale with a plain familiar limb-restraint proposal. Keep feasible positioning and airway support wording.

items.assessment: Intake/hydration recovery is meaningful, but medication-administration completion is a weak process distractor.
issues: Intake/hydration recovery is meaningful, but medication-administration completion is a weak process distractor.
proposedChanges: Replace that option with a clinical trend, such as unchanged concentrated urine or persistent postural tachycardia, so selection requires response interpretation.

items.assessment: Unknown placental location with late-pregnancy bleeding makes digital examination the specific action requiring clarification; other alternatives are relevant assessment steps.
Concealed abruption bleeding is a useful concept, but waiting-for-pad-measurement is not an interpretation and pain-alone is weak.
issues: Concealed abruption bleeding is a useful concept, but waiting-for-pad-measurement is not an interpretation and pain-alone is weak.
proposedChanges: Use parallel clinical interpretations or compare which observations best indicate severity despite limited external loss; keep blood-pressure/pulse and uterine findings central.

items.assessment: Possible ruptured ectopic pattern is appropriate, but routine ultrasound and waiting-for-heavier-bleeding are obvious delays.
issues: Possible ruptured ectopic pattern is appropriate, but routine ultrasound and waiting-for-heavier-bleeding are obvious delays.
proposedChanges: Use parallel possible causes/concerns or relevant assessment priorities; the task can ask which concern must be urgently excluded without asserting an independent nursing diagnosis.

items.assessment: The key is much longer and bundles the only reasonable response; every alternative is conspicuously unsafe. Generic within-training wording does not test a concrete action.
issues: The key is much longer and bundles the only reasonable response; every alternative is conspicuously unsafe. Generic within-training wording does not test a concrete action.
proposedChanges: Provide a brief authorized emergency protocol and role competence, then compare realistic pressure-relief/positioning/assessment actions. Avoid teaching cord replacement as the main distractor set.

items.assessment: The expanding-haematoma pattern is distinct and useful, but next-routine delay and walking-to-reduce-pressure are weak.
issues: The expanding-haematoma pattern is distinct and useful, but next-routine delay and walking-to-reduce-pressure are weak.
proposedChanges: Compare likely explanations such as haematoma, expected oedema, bladder distension and uterine atony, or identify the finding requiring urgent escalation.

items.assessment: Symptomatic glucose1.7mmol/L warrants immediate treatment, but sole skin-to-skin and every-low-reading-is-transitional are giveaway absolutes.
issues: Symptomatic glucose1.7mmol/L warrants immediate treatment, but sole skin-to-skin and every-low-reading-is-transitional are giveaway absolutes.
proposedChanges: Use an explicit newborn protocol and compare realistic treatment/confirmation/feeding steps while making clear that confirmatory testing cannot delay symptomatic treatment; do not inadvertently make a permitted interim dextrose-gel action false.

items.assessment: Oral feeding during major respiratory distress is unsafe; faster flow and flatter position are weak options.
issues: Oral feeding during major respiratory distress is unsafe; faster flow and flatter position are weak options.
proposedChanges: Use credible competing plans such as a smaller paced feed, temporary feed interruption with respiratory review, assessment of intake/weight, and discussion of alternative feeding support; keep one best immediate action.

items.assessment: Central tongue colour and feeding-related cardiopulmonary symptoms distinguish meaningful concerns from transient peripheral cooling and normal overall tolerance.
Preoperative fluid/electrolyte correction is valid, but spontaneous muscle relaxation and all-pain-disappeared options are implausible.
issues: Preoperative fluid/electrolyte correction is valid, but spontaneous muscle relaxation and all-pain-disappeared options are implausible.
proposedChanges: Compare physiological stabilization, aspiration-risk fasting, operative scheduling preparation, and nutritional recovery as parallel explanations; identify the actual dehydration/electrolyte context.

items.assessment: Intermittent intussusception pattern is useful, but larger-feed testing and wait-for-blood advertise unsafe care.
issues: Intermittent intussusception pattern is useful, but larger-feed testing and wait-for-blood advertise unsafe care.
proposedChanges: Use parallel interpretations such as colic, gastroenteritis, intermittent obstruction and reflux; timing, pallor and vomiting should distinguish the urgent concern.

items.assessment: Feeding/hydration support overlaps186 and the alternatives include improvised cereal and an entire-day delay.
issues: Feeding/hydration support overlaps186 and the alternatives include improvised cereal and an entire-day delay.
proposedChanges: Differentiate from186 by giving measured intake/urine trends and evaluating a prescribed assisted-feeding/hydration plan rather than repeating route review; use credible clinical alternatives.

items.assessment: Useful secretion-clearance outcome is appropriate, but procedure count and louder crying are weak process alternatives.
issues: Useful secretion-clearance outcome is appropriate, but procedure count and louder crying are weak process alternatives.
proposedChanges: Compare clinical response measures such as respiratory pauses, air entry, effort, oxygen need and feeding volume; mucus volume can remain as one plausible proxy error.

items.assessment: Discharge criteria are reasonable, but administrative observation timing is unrelated filler.
issues: Discharge criteria are reasonable, but administrative observation timing is unrelated filler.
proposedChanges: Replace with a plausible clinical/home-readiness proposal such as adequate saturation only while still receiving supplemental oxygen or a caregiver unable to maintain intake monitoring; avoid an only qualifier doing the discrimination.

items.assessment: Minimizing agitation is sound, but alone/flat/repeated tongue-depressor/every-nonurgent-first create cartoon care.
issues: Minimizing agitation is sound, but alone/flat/repeated tongue-depressor/every-nonurgent-first create cartoon care.
proposedChanges: Compare feasible examination approaches: parent-held upright assessment, brief separation for weighing, a supine exam, or completing observations in stages. Keep necessary urgent treatment explicit.

items.assessment: Quietening stridor with poorer air movement and drowsiness is a meaningful false-improvement pattern; the key explains deterioration rather than sound alone.
Transient epinephrine benefit is correct, but permanent airway change and positive viral test are implausible explanations.
issues: Transient epinephrine benefit is correct, but permanent airway change and positive viral test are implausible explanations.
proposedChanges: Use plausible observation purposes such as recurrence after drug effect, response to coadministered steroid, feeding tolerance, or adverse-effect monitoring; ask specifically why immediate symptom relief alone is insufficient.

items.assessment: Airway-protective handling is clinically appropriate, but all three wrong choices combine provocative manoeuvres with delay.
issues: Airway-protective handling is clinically appropriate, but all three wrong choices combine provocative manoeuvres with delay.
proposedChanges: Use plausible competing assessment actions such as noninvasive observations, expert airway activation, parent-held positioning and arranging investigations; specify the priority boundary so only one response leads.

items.assessment: Small measured volumes are appropriate, but rest-of-day withholding and rapid catchup are conspicuously extreme.
issues: Small measured volumes are appropriate, but rest-of-day withholding and rapid catchup are conspicuously extreme.
proposedChanges: Use realistic delivery alternatives such as smaller frequent portions, a longer pause before retrying the same cup, switching solution taste/formulation, or changing the scheduled total; preserve explicit mild dehydration and reassessment.

items.assessment: Changed systemic pattern warrants review; a meal trial is implausible in known appendicitis and routine-delay wording telegraphs error.
issues: Changed systemic pattern warrants review; a meal trial is implausible in known appendicitis and routine-delay wording telegraphs error.
proposedChanges: Ask for interpretation of the pain-location/systemic trend with parallel competing explanations; keep possible perforation rather than definitive diagnosis.

items.assessment: Torsion recognition is time-sensitive and useful, but next-morning strain treatment and constipation-first are weak.
issues: Torsion recognition is time-sensitive and useful, but next-morning strain treatment and constipation-first are weak.
proposedChanges: Use parallel concerns or credible focused assessments without arbitrary delay clauses; retain the private history that reveals the relevant symptom.

items.assessment: Neurological deterioration during DKA treatment is important, but reduced observation and assumed first-meal intolerance are weak.
issues: Neurological deterioration during DKA treatment is important, but reduced observation and assumed first-meal intolerance are weak.
proposedChanges: Use parallel possible complications or clinically relevant urgent actions with clear timing. Differentiate from the adult DKA electrolyte/insulin items through neurological trend interpretation, not just generic emergency escalation.
